origins.section: An Implicitly Typed Lambda Can't Choose Between Overloads of the Same Arity
When a Body Fits Both, the Overload That Returns a Value Wins
A Body's Shape Decides Whether It Returns a Value, Nothing, or Either
A Lambda Can't Implement a Generic Method

gates.says: all 4 of this quiz's answerable readings held and each was taken over the question as it stands

recorded.prompt:q-var-overload: the page and the question, and nothing else
recorded.pass:q-var-overload: independent readers: a page-free reader (wording only) and a page reader with the page and the quiz, each a fresh agent
recorded.outcome:q-var-overload: Option c is decided. L159-161: "for an implicitly typed lambda javac checks only the body's shape. An expression body might return a value, so it fits both ... Without declared types the value-returning preference doesn't apply, so the call is ambiguous. `(var m) -> ack(m)` is ambiguous too." L47: "`var` ... still counts as inferred." L220-221: "to overload resolution it is still inferred." L172-173 gives the same-shaped ToIntFunction/Function pair as ambiguous.
recorded.prompt:q-submit-remove: the page and the question, and nothing else
recorded.pass:q-submit-remove: independent readers: a page-free reader (wording only) and a page reader with the page and the quiz, each a fresh agent
recorded.outcome:q-submit-remove: Option b is decided. L125-126: "When a body fits both and its parameter types are known (declared, or there are none, as here), the compiler prefers the interface whose method returns a value. `submit` does the same." L129/L135: `pool.submit(() -> seen.add("o-7"))` gives `get() = true`. L55-59: a method call fits both void and value targets.
recorded.prompt:q-label-paths: the page and the question, and nothing else
recorded.pass:q-label-paths: independent readers: a page-free reader (wording only) and a page reader with the page and the quiz, each a fresh agent
recorded.outcome:q-label-paths: Option c is decided. L66-67: value-compatible needs "every `return` carries one and control can't reach the closing brace." L72-75 has the same pattern (`somePaths`, two ifs, no final return), and L88-91 shows javac rejecting it with "bad return type in lambda expression ... missing return value". L98: "`somePaths` falls off its end for a two-letter string."
recorded.prompt:q-generic-converter: the page and the question, and nothing else
recorded.pass:q-generic-converter: independent readers: a page-free reader (wording only) and a page reader with the page and the quiz, each a fresh agent
recorded.outcome:q-generic-converter: Option c is decided. L197-203: javac rejects the lambda with "invalid functional descriptor for lambda expression ... method <T>(T,T)T in interface Picker is generic". L205-206: "A lambda has nowhere to declare `<T>`. A method reference to a generic method fits, and so does an anonymous class." L211 shows `GenericRef::larger`.

recorded.prompt:q-var-overload:a: the page and the question, and nothing else
recorded.pass:q-var-overload:a: independent readers: a page-free reader (wording only) and a page reader with the page and the quiz, each a fresh agent
recorded.outcome:q-var-overload:a: Ruled out by L47 ("`var` ... still counts as inferred"), L161 ("`(var m) -> ack(m)` is ambiguous too") and L220-221.
recorded.prompt:q-var-overload:b: the page and the question, and nothing else
recorded.pass:q-var-overload:b: independent readers: a page-free reader (wording only) and a page reader with the page and the quiz, each a fresh agent
recorded.outcome:q-var-overload:b: Ruled out by L159-161: for an implicitly typed lambda javac checks only the body's shape; an expression body fits both, so the call is ambiguous. L170-171 says only declared types let the compiler check the body's type.
recorded.prompt:q-var-overload:d: the page and the question, and nothing else
recorded.pass:q-var-overload:d: independent readers: a page-free reader (wording only) and a page reader with the page and the quiz, each a fresh agent
recorded.outcome:q-var-overload:d: Ruled out only indirectly. L161 says `(var m) -> ack(m)` is ambiguous, so the reported failure is ambiguity, not an invalid use of `var`. The page never shows a bare `var` parameter compiling, and L46-47 ("`var` exists to allow them") could be read as backing d's premise.
recorded.prompt:q-submit-remove:a: the page and the question, and nothing else
recorded.pass:q-submit-remove:a: independent readers: a page-free reader (wording only) and a page reader with the page and the quiz, each a fresh agent
recorded.outcome:q-submit-remove:a: Ruled out by L55-59 (a call like `seen.add(...)` fits both kinds of target), L110/L118 (`seen.add("x")` -> Callable) and L129/L135 (get() = true). Having no `return` statement doesn't make an expression body a Runnable.
recorded.prompt:q-submit-remove:c: the page and the question, and nothing else
recorded.pass:q-submit-remove:c: independent readers: a page-free reader (wording only) and a page reader with the page and the quiz, each a fresh agent
recorded.outcome:q-submit-remove:c: Ruled out by L125-126 ("prefers the interface whose method returns a value") and L224-225.
recorded.prompt:q-submit-remove:d: the page and the question, and nothing else
recorded.pass:q-submit-remove:d: independent readers: a page-free reader (wording only) and a page reader with the page and the quiz, each a fresh agent
recorded.outcome:q-submit-remove:d: Ruled out by putting L111/L119 (a braced body -> Runnable) together with L130/L136 (braced submit gives `get() = null`), plus L140 ("Adding braces turned a `Future` holding `true` into one holding `null`"). The page doesn't state outright that a Runnable's Future returns null; the reader has to infer it from these lines.
